title: control-plane: add RolloutPlan/Stage/Gate schema + migrations + validation
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: Dedicated pools currently rely on pool-level, mostly all-at-once changes. This PR introduces the foundational control-plane schema for staged rollouts (RolloutPlan -> Stages -> Gates) so subsequent PRs can add CRUD APIs, evaluator, and routing integration. Scope: (1) Protobuf + internal schema definitions for RolloutPlan/Stage/Gate and related enums; (2) Persistence scaffolding (DB migration + ORM mapping) including optimistic concurrency fields; (3) Server-side validation rules (static validation at write time) to keep plans well-formed and safe; (4) Minimal read-path plumbing behind a feature flag so we can start writing integration tests in staging without exposing UI/API yet. Key design notes: RolloutPlan is tenant-scoped and may optionally bind to a dedicated_pool_id (v1 is Dedicated-only, but schema keeps room for future deployment targets). Stages are ordered and have a weight_percent that is enforced by routing (future PR), plus an evaluation_window and approval_policy. Gates are per-stage and reference a metric signal (e.g., p95 latency, 5xx rate, queue depth) with threshold + operator. Validation is conservative: if config is ambiguous or unsafe, reject writes rather than attempting to coerce. Safety/constraints validated: stage weights must be monotonic non-decreasing and end at 100; stage ids must be unique and stable; max number of stages and gates enforced to control cardinality; evaluation_window must be within min/max; disallow gate configs that would require high-cardinality dimensions; require dedicated_pool_id for Dedicated rollout plans; disallow editing an active plan unless providing expected_resource_version (optimistic concurrency). Proto sketch (abbrev): message RolloutPlan { string id; string tenant_id; string dedicated_pool_id; string name; RolloutTarget target; repeated Stage stages; int64 resource_version; google.protobuf.Timestamp created_at; google.protobuf.Timestamp updated_at; } message Stage { string id; int32 order; int32 weight_percent; EvaluationWindow window; ApprovalPolicy approval_policy; repeated Gate gates; } message Gate { string id; GateType type; Comparator comparator; double threshold; int32 min_sample_size; } Follow-ups: ENG-5122 will add rollout CRUD endpoints and approval/abort, ENG-5124 will add evaluator, ENG-5123 will apply weights in routing. Testing: unit tests for validation and migration smoke tests are included; end-to-end tests will land once APIs exist. Rollout: schema and migrations are behind dedicated_staged_rollouts_enabled=false by default; migration is additive and safe to deploy before any writers are enabled.
commits: control-plane/proto: introduce rollout_plan.proto with Stage/Gate messages
control-plane/schema: add RolloutPlan ORM + resource_version for optimistic concurrency
validation: enforce stage ordering, weights, and gate constraints
tests: validation unit tests + migration smoke test
review_conversation: Ethan Park (review): Overall direction looks right. Two things: (1) please make sure stage.order is derived from array order OR enforce strict uniqueness/contiguous ordering; (2) we need to be explicit about whether weight_percent is absolute (traffic to new) vs incremental per-stage. Benji Okafor (author): Good call. I updated validation to require contiguous ordering starting at 0 and clarified in proto comments: weight_percent is absolute traffic allocated to the new candidate at that stage. Michael Nguyen (review): For resource_version, please confirm how writers will do compare-and-swap. Also, migration creates rollout_plan_events but we don’t use it yet; ok to keep but make sure retention/indexing is sane. Benji Okafor (author): Added docstring + TODO for ENG-5122: APIs will require If-Match/expected_resource_version. For events table I added (tenant_id, plan_id, created_at) index and kept payload as jsonb for now; retention policy will be in audit logging PR. Jordan Lee (review): Determinism concerns: stage ids must be stable and not regenerated on edit, otherwise routing hash buckets will churn. Can we enforce stage.id immutability on update? Benji Okafor (author): Added update validation: existing stage ids must be preserved; only append is allowed unless plan is not active (future state machine). For now we reject edits if plan is in ACTIVE/PAUSED (state enum stubbed). Kaitlyn Nguyen (review): RBAC isn’t here yet, but please ensure tenant_id is required and never derived from request body in later APIs. Also, any PII in events? Benji Okafor (author): tenant_id required at schema layer; added comment + validation that tenant_id cannot be empty. Events payload intentionally excludes actor info for now; audit logging will be separate and uses structured event schema (ENG-5128/ADR-028). Marcus Lin (review): From a compliance/audit perspective, avoid storing arbitrary configs without bounds. The max stages/gates limits are good; can you also cap name length and require gate.min_sample_size bounds? Benji Okafor (author): Done: name max 128 chars, stage count max 8, gates per stage max 10, min_sample_size [10, 100000]. Ethan Park (final): LGTM after the contiguous ordering change + comment clarifications. Approved. Michael Nguyen (final): Approved. Jordan Lee (final): Approved after stage id immutability validation. Merged via squash.
security_notes: No customer data paths changed. New tables are additive and empty unless feature flag is enabled. Validation limits reduce risk of unbounded config / high-cardinality gates. Audit actor fields are intentionally not introduced in this PR; tracked in ENG-5128 with ADR-028.
testing_notes: Added validation unit tests for stage ordering/weights, gate thresholds/sample size, and name length; migration smoke test validates tables/indexes apply cleanly in CI.
deployment_notes: Safe to deploy ahead of writers/readers. Feature flag dedicated_staged_rollouts_enabled defaults false; tables created but unused until subsequent API PRs.
